title: Curve testing for geometric irreducibility
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq1$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, with
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let
$\mathcal S_1,\ldots,\mathcal S_r$ be $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves on $X_0$ whose
geometric restrictions to $X$ are irreducible local systems. Let $S$ be
a nonempty finite set of $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-points of $X$. There
are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$
and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains $S$,
such that every $i^*\mathcal S_j$ is an irreducible local system on $C$,
and $C$ is defined over a finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$:
there is an automorphism $\varphi$ of $C$ with
$i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$, where
$\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius of
$X$.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$; it is chosen in Step 5 as $i\circ\bar c$ for a geometric point $\bar c$ of the curve, and a change of base point changes every representation below only by conjugation, which preserves irreducibility and images up to conjugation. For each $j$, use [def-wf-fundamental-representation] to encode the geometric restriction of $\mathcal S_j$ by its continuous representation of $\pi_1(X)$. The finite-stage convention in [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] allows all these representations and their invariant lattices to be chosen over finite coefficient fields. The assumed geometric irreducibility is exactly absolute irreducibility after extending those fields to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

Apply [lem-zl-finite-matrix-irreducibility] to each representation. It supplies an integer $N_j\ge1$ and a finite reduction quotient of the chosen lattice such that any subgroup of $\pi_1(X)$ with the same image in that quotient still acts absolutely irreducibly on the corresponding representation.

Intersect the finitely many open normal kernels of these reduction quotients. The intersection is open and normal, so its quotient is a finite group $Q$. By the finite-etale/fundamental-group equivalence [thm-galois-fundamental] (equivalently the open-subgroup description [cor-galois-open-subgroups]), the regular finite $Q$-set gives a connected finite etale Galois cover $T\to X$ whose geometric monodromy quotient is $Q$.

source.place: proof, sentences beginning “Intersect their open normal kernels”

proof.text: Assume $d\ge2$. The scheme $X$ is smooth, affine, of dimension $d$ over the algebraically closed field $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and connected because $X_0$ is geometrically connected; $T$ is connected and finite etale over $X$ by Step 3, and $S\subset X(\overline{\mathbf F}_q)$ is finite and nonempty. Apply [lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve] to $X$, $T\to X$ and $S$. We obtain a smooth connected affine closed curve $C\subset X$ containing $S$, with inclusion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$, such that $T\times_XC$ is connected, and the curve and its inclusion are defined over some $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$: $C=C_1\times_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $i=i_1\times\mathrm{id}$ for a closed immersion $i_1:C_1\hookrightarrow X_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\mathbf F_{q^m}$. Put $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{C_1}\times\sigma^m$, an automorphism of $C$. Since $(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m=\mathrm{id}_{X_0\times\mathbf F_{q^m}}\times\sigma^m$ on $X=(X_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\mathbf F_{q^m})\times_{\mathbf F_{q^m}}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, we get $i\circ\varphi=i_1\times\sigma^m=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$. (The main-20261015 form of [lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve] states this equation directly.)

Choose a geometric point $\bar c$ of $C$ and put $\bar x=i\circ\bar c$ (the base point of Step 1). The connected finite etale cover $T\times_XC\to C$ is a connected object of the finite-etale Galois category by [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object]. Hence [lem-galois-transitive] and [thm-galois-fundamental] identify the image of $\pi_1(C)$ in $Q$ with a transitive subgroup of the regular $Q$-set $Q$, so that image is all of $Q$. In particular it has the same image as $\pi_1(X)$ in every reduction quotient.

source.place: proof, sentences beginning “Connectedness of the restricted $Q$-torsor”

proof.text: For each $j$, the subgroup $\Pi'=\operatorname{im}(i_*:\pi_1(C,\bar c)\to\pi_1(X,\bar x))$ has, by Step 5, the same image as $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ in $\operatorname{GL}(L_j/\varpi^{N_j}L_j)$, since that reduction quotient is a quotient of $Q$. Hence [lem-zl-finite-matrix-irreducibility] shows that $\Pi'$ acts absolutely irreducibly on $V_j$. The geometric representation of $i^*\mathcal S_j$ at $\bar c$ is $\rho_{j,\mathrm{geom}}\circ i_*$: the stalk $(i^*\mathcal S_j)_{\bar c}$ is $(\mathcal S_j)_{\bar x}$, and at every finite level $L_j/\varpi^nL_j$ the base-change clause of [thm-galois-fundamental] ($|(P\times_XC)_{\bar c}|\cong|P_{\bar x}|$ as $\pi_1(C,\bar c)$-sets through $i_*$) identifies the action, which by [def-wf-fundamental-representation] is how the geometric representation is formed. So the representation of $i^*\mathcal S_j$ is absolutely irreducible, i.e. $i^*\mathcal S_j$ is an irreducible local system on $C$.

source.place: proof, sentences beginning “It surjects onto each chosen reduction quotient”

proof.text: The Frobenius-stable curve and immersion supplied by [lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve] descend to the finite field $\mathbf F_{q^m}$; the original Weil descent data restrict along the Frobenius automorphism $\varphi$, so each $i^*\mathcal S_j$ inherits its Weil structure over that field. This is the finite-presentation descent and restriction of the defining Weil datum in [def-wf-fundamental-representation].

source.place: proof, sentences beginning “The curve and inclusion descend”

proof.text: If $d=1$, take $C=X$ and $i=\mathrm{id}_X$; the identity curve is smooth, connected and affine, every restriction is unchanged, and the geometric Frobenius itself supplies the required automorphism (take $m=1$).

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq1$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, with
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let
$\mathcal S_1,\ldots,\mathcal S_r$ be $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves on $X_0$ whose
geometric restrictions to $X$ are irreducible local systems. Let $S$ be
a nonempty finite set of $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-points of $X$. There
are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$
and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains $S$,
such that every $i^*\mathcal S_j$ is an irreducible local system on $C$,
and $C$ is defined over a finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$:
there is an automorphism $\varphi$ of $C$ with
$i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$, where
$\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius of
$X$.

proof.text:
Use the geometric representations of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation], and choose finite coefficient
fields for them as allowed in [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category].
By [lem-zl-finite-matrix-irreducibility], each has a finite
reduction quotient detecting absolute irreducibility. Intersect
their open normal kernels in $\pi_1(X)$, where
$X=X_0\times\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. The resulting finite quotient
$Q$ corresponds to a connected finite etale Galois cover $T\to X$.
For $\dim X\geq2$, apply
[lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve]. Connectedness of the
restricted $Q$-torsor means that the image of $\pi_1(C)$ acts
transitively on $Q$, hence is all of $Q$. It surjects onto each
chosen reduction quotient. The finite matrix witnesses show that
all the restricted geometric representations remain irreducible.
The curve and inclusion descend to a finite constant extension;
the restrictions inherit their Weil structures over that field.
For dimension one take $C=X$, with its given finite-field model.

split_report.blueprint: Realizes the complete proof of main-20261015 blueprint node lem-zl-curve-testing-irreducibility: the representation and finite-witness sentences (steps 1–2), quotient-cover construction (step 3), Bertini sentence (step 4), connected-torsor monodromy and matrix conclusion (steps 5–6), finite-field descent (step 7), and dimension-one case (step 8).

tool_uses.why: The finite quotient Q is converted into a finite-etale cover and its fibre action is identified with the fundamental-group action.
The open-subgroup classification supplies the connected cover associated with the normal kernel.
Connectedness of the pulled-back finite-etale scheme is converted to connectedness in the Galois category.
The connected finite-etale object has a transitive fundamental-group action on its geometric fibre.
